problems.statement: Pay alone is the cause of the turnover surge, so a 15% across-the-board raise is the fix.
A pay gap versus local competitors is a real contributor, especially to hiring and to some exits, but its size is unknown because there has been no market study since 2023.

Schedule burden is a main contributor to the step-up from March 2026. The all-branch Saturday change (two Saturdays a month, hours extended to 15:00) took effect 2026-03-02, the ShiftWise rollout was announced to all tellers on 2026-03-04, and schedule/hours citations rose from 19% to 48%.
ShiftWise itself, as live at 19 branches, is the main driver of excess exits.

A tightening labor market raised baseline turnover. Exits were already about 11 a month in Oct-Feb, against 7.2 a month the prior Oct-Mar, before either schedule change, and peer banks rose 5 points. Cedar Hollow rose far more, so the market explains only part of the increase.

Poor branch managers drive turnover. This is currently unsupported by usable data: the manager-of-record field is stale for the 7 branches that changed managers, 3 of the 5 named branches changed manager mid-year, and the survey manager option has no baseline.
The surge is a measurement artifact of the HRIS migration or of how separations were counted.

A vacancy and churn loop amplifies the problem. Open requisitions drive covering overtime, and the share of leavers with under 12 months' tenure rose from 41% to 58%. Time-to-fill rose to 41 days and offer acceptance fell to 79%.

causalClaims.to: The rise in teller turnover from 28% to 47%
Step-up in voluntary exits from March
Higher turnover at ShiftWise branches than elsewhere

actions.action: Approve the 15% across-the-board teller raise before the December 10 budget lock.
actions.rationale: It costs about $2.6M a year and is not practically reversible. Pay was cited at similar rates in both years (58% vs 61%) while turnover rose about 70%, and schedule changes coincide with the step-up.

actions.action: Request the branch-level separation report with corrected manager-of-record dates (ready about 2026-12-01), split by ShiftWise vs non-ShiftWise branch and before vs after March 2026.
actions.rationale: It is cheap, arrives before the budget lock, and tests the manager, ShiftWise and Saturday explanations directly.

actions.action: Buy the State Bankers Association 2026 teller pay module or commission a quick market check, and compare it with the roughly $18.50-$20.00 postings.
actions.rationale: The bank does not know where it sits against the market. Without that, neither the size of any raise nor the case against one can be set.

actions.action: Hold the broad raise for now, and preserve the option of a targeted adjustment (for example, the starting rate or specific markets) through the January 2027 cycle, which needs approval by 2027-01-05.
actions.rationale: This keeps pay on the table once the market data is in, at far lower cost and with less irreversibility than a 15% increase.

actions.action: Withhold bonuses from, or put on performance-improvement plans, the managers named by the Regional VP using the PeopleCore manager field.
actions.rationale: The field is stale for the 7 branches that changed managers, and 3 of the 5 named branches changed manager mid-year. The selection rests on anecdote, and the action risks punishing the wrong people and worsening attrition.

actions.action: Delay the ShiftWise expansion to the other 27 branches (scheduled 2027-01-11; the date can be moved with 30 days' notice at no fee) until branch data is in. In the interim, review the 7-day posting window and manager schedule control.
actions.rationale: This is cheap and reversible. ShiftWise has not been shown to cause excess exits, but staff cite schedule unpredictability and the evidence is thin.

actions.action: Review the second-Saturday and extended Saturday hours policy, for example with voluntary swaps or a rotation, and pilot a longer posting lead time.
actions.rationale: Schedule citations and the March timing point to it, but the causal link is unconfirmed, so a pilot should come before a wholesale reversal.

actions.action: Collect structured exit and stay interviews, and track turnover by tenure cohort.
actions.rationale: The 19% survey response rate is low and the manager option has no baseline, so the survey cannot settle the cause.

nextEvidence: Separations by branch with corrected manager-of-record dates, split ShiftWise vs non-ShiftWise and before vs after 2026-03-02 and 2026-04-13 (HR Analytics, about 2026-12-01)
Current local market pay data for tellers (State Bankers Association 2026 pay module or equivalent) benchmarked against the $17.60 starting rate
Leaver-level destination and reason data from exit or stay interviews, including whether they moved to higher pay and which branch and schedule they left
output.summary: The surge is not shown to be a pure pay problem. Pay was cited at similar rates in both years (58% and 61%), while schedule/hours citations rose from 19% to 48%. Exits stepped up in March 2026, when the all-branch second-Saturday policy and the ShiftWise announcement landed, and ShiftWise branches show no excess. A tighter labor market explains part of the baseline rise. Pay is a likely but unsized contributor, since there has been no market study since 2023. Manager blame rests on stale data. Do not approve the 15% raise or punish managers now. Get branch-level data and a market benchmark before December 10, and keep a targeted January adjustment available.
